subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must extend a declared constant-rate relation to a value outside the given data
use when a prediction is made by pattern-spotting rather than by applying a stated rate
anchor: Extrapolation is a declared linear model applied outside the observed range: predicted value equals a known value plus the constant rate times the change in input.
ordinary_language_bridge: Say 'each extra unit of input changes the output by this much' and then count how many extra units are needed.
reconstruction_route: identify the input and output quantities and their units
compute the constant rate from two known pairs
state the rate in words with its units
measure the change in input from a known point to the target
add the rate multiplied by that change to the known output
state the assumption that the rate stays constant outside the data

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: the same two data pairs and the same target input
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: applying the rate to the change in input versus to the target input itself
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: How many extra input units separate the known point from the target?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: the rate multiplies the change in input, not the raw input value

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: extrapolation continues a visible number pattern regardless of step size
misconception_discriminator.probe: use unequal input steps so that pattern-continuation and rate-application disagree
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner applies the rate to the actual input difference

repair_route: recompute the rate from matched differences
recompute the input change to the target
retry on a target below the observed range
verification_method: predict a known data value with the same model and compare with the given value
check that the units of the prediction match the output quantity
known_limitations: does not justify that the relation is linear beyond the declared model
does not quantify uncertainty of the prediction
